notes: Fewer wasted requests: a contact who is a junior specialist, coordinator or assistant, or a board member or investor, is now set aside automatically with the reason, so requests only go to founders and marketing leads.

Fewer wrong people: the LinkedIn person finder now only picks someone whose headline names the brand right next to their founder or marketing title, so a person who just mentions a word like Azure, or runs a firm with a similar name, is no longer chosen.
Not relevant now works in one click: press Not relevant, then click the reason, and the lead is gone for good. A lead you remove never comes back to Ready to send, even if they reply later.

Reports: the first column now counts brands you can actually send a request to (Ready to contact), not every brand the search looked at. Hover a number to see how many were checked and what the search cost. A dash means no search was needed because enough brands were queued.
Reports no longer shows today's requests in red before sending starts. Requests go out from 1pm to 11pm UK (US business hours), and the Requests today tile now says so.
New: about an hour after someone accepts, they automatically get a short "video on its way" message, so the conversation starts while the video is being made. Switch it off in Settings, LinkedIn.
Every video is now due 48 hours after they accept. Ready to send cards count down, turn red when late, and the 9am text lists late ones first.
Anyone who replies before their video stays on Ready to send, with their reply shown on the card.
Replies are now read properly. A bug meant the AI never saw the actual words of a reply, so Positive and Neutral labels were guesses. Fixed, and every stored reply has been read again.

The grey 'no image' boxes on prospects were Meta ad pictures whose links had expired (Meta only keeps them a few days). They now say 'Preview expired' and each ad has a 'See this ad on Meta' link that always works.
Replies are read more strictly: a simple thank you, or someone selling us their own services, no longer counts as a positive reply.
Article and quiz pages from a brand's ads are no longer picked as the product to film.
Every number in Reports is clickable: it opens the prospect list showing just those leads, with what we sent them and what they replied.
Each Reports column has a ? bubble explaining what it counts.
Reports now colour each weekday green when on target and red when something needs fixing, with a Today scorecard at the top.
New brands are found sooner: the system keeps two days of sending queued and can search twice a day.
Every weekday at 9am you get a text listing the connections waiting for a video.
The Reports table now fits on screen without scrolling sideways.
Reports is now in the left menu under Video Outreach, next to Ask AI and Help and guide.

Second LinkedIn sender: Settings, LinkedIn senders has a Connect another LinkedIn button that creates a secure Unipile sign-in link to send to the person. Once they sign in, their LinkedIn sends its own connection requests from the same queue (never the same person twice), with its own daily cap, and the video message and follow-ups to their contacts go from their account, signed with their name.

Safer targeting: board members, investors, advisers and former staff are no longer picked as a brand's contact, and very high-profile people (over 25,000 LinkedIn followers) are skipped before any request goes out.

New Reports tab in Video Outreach: a day-by-day table of connection requests, acceptances, videos sent, follow-ups and replies, plus what became of each day's requests. Last 31 days by default, Show more for older days, click a day to see the brands, and download as CSV.

Fixed: connection requests had stopped since 1 October because LinkedIn refused a repeat invitation to someone whose old request had been withdrawn, and the queue waited on that one person. Now nobody is invited twice, and if LinkedIn refuses one person the next one is sent instead.

Ready to send: each lead now has a 'Get contact details' button. Press it to look up the decision maker's verified email and phone from Apollo (founder or CEO first, then a marketing lead), saved onto the card. It only runs when you press it, so it spends credits on purpose. Mobiles can take a few minutes to come back from Apollo.
The Help flowchart now shows the run as two steps: 'Find brands' (pulls brands from Meta) and 'Analyse & draft' (scores them, reads the website and store, picks the product and writes the messages).
Ready to send cards are tidier: a clear 'Your video' section and 'The message' section, more spacing, and a bigger Send on LinkedIn button.

The Help and guide 'The whole loop' is now a simple flowchart, with each step numbered, green for what runs on its own and amber for where you step in, and small Meta, Instagram, LinkedIn and ScrollyVid tiles on the right steps.
Ready to send: your uploaded videos now show the whole video upright and larger, instead of a cropped slice. Portrait videos were being chopped into a small landscape box.
Deep Dossier now finds real people from Apollo, with verified work emails and office numbers.
New LinkedIn activity filter: keep only people who have been quiet on LinkedIn for 6 or 12 months (or only active ones). Each profile is checked live, and you can see who was left out and why.

Mobiles and direct lines are fetched from Apollo and fill into the table on their own within a few minutes. Numbers on the do-not-call register are flagged. Everything is saved to Our Leads and the CSV and PDF exports.
Every Ready to send card has a Not relevant button. Pick the reason, add a note if you like, and the lead leaves the list and gets no messages.
Analytics has a Marked not relevant table counting the reasons, so we can see what the search keeps getting wrong.
The LinkedIn activity check now looks at comments as well as posts, so someone who comments often but rarely posts counts as active.
Behind the scenes: SitePounce can now check how recently any LinkedIn profile has posted or commented. It is used for a client proof of concept; a screen for it in Deep Dossier comes later.
Behind the scenes: Automation Growth Lab can now text Ajay's alert mobile through the SitePounce number, for example when someone asks for the free setup. Nothing in the SitePounce app changes.

Product names in the message are tidied to sound human, not like a web page title: SEO tails, codes, sizes and counts are removed and capitals are softened. For example 'EKKOLYTE - Electrolytes and Minerals' becomes Ekkolyte.
The Product in the video box shows the same tidied name the message uses.

SitePounce now reads a brand's whole online shop, not just the first 50 products, and the product their ads are pushing is always the one suggested to film. For EKKO that is Ekkolyte, the electrolyte powder in their ads.
An Update message button sits next to Product in the video. Clicking away still updates it too, and if you edited the message yourself your edits are kept and only the product wording changes.
Each Ready to send card has a Product in the video box. SitePounce fills in its pick; type the product you actually filmed and click away, and the message updates with that name.
When the video is of a different product than the one in their ads, the message no longer says 'so': it reads as two plain sentences.

Each Ready to send card has a cross next to the Video URL box to take the video off the message or delete it. The uploaded video always shows under the box with its Delete button, and if something stops the list loading, the card now says why.
The video message can no longer be sent twice to the same person. Once it has gone, the Send button disappears from the lead's page and the follow-ups take over.
A lead's own page (click Open) also lists its uploaded videos, so you can delete a spare one after the message has gone. The video that was sent is kept, because the follow-ups link to it.

Each Ready to send card now shows the videos uploaded for that lead, with a small player. The one marked On the message is the one that gets sent: click Use this one to switch, or the Delete cross to remove a wrong or duplicate upload.
Long product names are shortened in the message (for example 'Daily Ultimate Essentials Pro' instead of the full store title with a subtitle).

The product picked to film is always a real product: refills, upgrades, add-ons, free gifts, clearance lines and items the store hides are skipped, and a single product beats a multi-pack. IM8 Health now gets Daily Ultimate Essentials Pro.
The video message no longer repeats the product name when their ads already named it.

The video message is rewritten to sound personal and short: it thanks them for connecting, names their ads, says your team made the sample, offers more daily or weekly and asks for a day and time. It is signed Aj only, with no title, because every message goes out from Ajay's LinkedIn whoever presses Send.
Robotic phrases about their ads (for example 'showcasing ... effectively') are removed.
The picture of your screen in Feedback now takes about a second and no longer freezes the page.
Feedback opens straight away. The picture of your screen fills in while you type, instead of making you wait.

Ready to send: stores that redirect by country (like Myzone) are now read, so a product is picked. A brand with no online shop says what their site sells and has a Not a fit button, and brands without a real shop no longer get through.
Video Outreach has a new Sent tab with every video and follow-up sent and the follow-ups booked next. Ready to send shows the last one sent at the top.
The Feedback button is now bottom-right (the menu used to hide it) and gives a small bounce now and then. Each note includes a picture of your screen, the version and any error you just hit.
The version number now shows clearly at the bottom of the menu. Click it to see what changed.
Ready to send, the help page and the error messages now say video link instead of naming the tool the video was made with.

Follow-up 3 now uses the brand's own country calendar, worked out on the day it sends. US brands hear about Thanksgiving, the 4th of July and Labor Day; UK and Irish brands get Black Friday and Mother's Day (Mothering Sunday, three weeks before Easter) and never Thanksgiving; Canada, Australia and New Zealand have their own dates; anywhere else only dates every market shares.
Every contacted brand now gets its missing follow-ups booked automatically. A follow-up you skip is never put back.
Ready to send has a Scheduled follow-ups list: brand, which follow-up, due date and the message as it reads today, with Open and Skip.

Follow-up 3 names a real US occasion from a calendar (Thanksgiving and Black Friday, Christmas, new year, Valentine's Day, Mother's Day, Memorial Day, Father's Day, 4th of July, Labor Day, Halloween), worked out at the moment of sending. The big shopping moments come first, and only one 14 to 75 days ahead is ever named, so it can never mention an occasion that has passed; otherwise it says Ahead of your next campaign.
Find on LinkedIn runs one brand every 20 minutes instead of every 10, to stay well inside LinkedIn's search limits.

Find on LinkedIn also accepts the people who buy creative (creative strategists and directors, brand, content, ecommerce and marketing managers) when no founder or marketing head is found. Founders still come first; editors, freelancers and creators are never picked. Brands missed so far are searched again.
Find on LinkedIn reports what each search and profile check returned, so a miss can be explained.

Follow-ups spread out: Follow-up 1 on day 4, Follow-up 2 on day 12, so someone away for a week does not come back to a pile of messages. New last Follow-up 3, 30 days after Follow-up 2, with a seasonal reason (Black Friday, Christmas, new year) offering a second free sample for their next product. Any reply cancels it.

Warm-up like test: half the people ready for a request get a like on their newest LinkedIn post first and the request a day later, the other half get it straight away. At most 25 likes a day. Analytics shows the acceptance of both halves; the switch is in Settings, LinkedIn caps.

Two people per brand: when the contact has not posted or commented on LinkedIn in 90 days, the worker looks for another founder or marketing lead at the same brand (Apollo's second contact first) and switches the request to them once they pass the activity check. The first contact is kept on the record.

LinkedIn person search, second version: the brand goes in quotes with founder, CEO or marketing (LinkedIn's title filter returned nothing), and when a result's headline does not name the brand its current job on the profile is checked. Brands the first version marked as nobody found are searched again once.
LinkedIn person search retries on the brand name alone when the job-title filter returns nothing.

Second way to find the person: when Apollo finds nobody at a shortlisted brand, the worker searches LinkedIn itself for a founder or marketing lead who works there, one brand every 10 minutes. A Find on LinkedIn button on the prospect page does the same on demand. Automation health shows how many it searched and found.

Automatic follow-ups switched on for both campaigns. Safety rules first: one follow-up per person per run (overdue ones no longer stack), Follow-up 2 at least 4 days after Follow-up 1, LinkedIn follow-ups only in US business hours and under the daily message cap.
Follow-ups open with Hey and the first name instead of bolting the name onto a sentence, and the offer line no longer says for supplement brands.
The funnel never shows blank: a date range with nothing in it falls back to the last 90 days, then all time, and says so.
Funnel has a date range: last 30 days by default, pick any from and to dates, or All time, so earlier periods can be compared.
Funnel table gains an Of all scanned column, so every stage reads as a percentage of the brands scanned.

Analytics has a Funnel table: brands scanned, shortlisted, found on LinkedIn, active, requests sent, accepted, videos sent, replies, positive, calls, each with its percentage, and a Copy button for WhatsApp.
Daily activity graph day labels fixed.
Sending now runs first in every worker run, on its own. Since 22 September the checks that come before it (thousands of connections, profile lookups) used up the run and the send never happened.
Results is now Analytics, with an Automation health block that says in plain words what the last worker run did and why nothing was sent, and a 14-day daily activity graph.
Automatic top-ups are one run a day per campaign (was up to three) and only when fewer than 12 brands are ready to request, to keep sourcing cost near £5 a day.

Watchdog texts: you and Aryan get a text the moment the automation pauses, when finding new brands fails (once a day), and at the end of any weekday on which no connection request went out. The 14 September stop went unnoticed for a week because it only sent an email.
Video compression measures the clip inside the encoder instead of waiting on the browser's video player, which could hang in a background tab.
Video compression starts reliably: the encoder receives its engine bytes directly instead of fetching them by path.
Video compression runs the encoder in SitePounce's own worker, so it starts reliably from the CDN.
Video compression loads the right build of the compressor (it failed to start in 1.5.29).

Ready to send: Upload a video file from your computer (mp4, mov or webm). Anything over 20 MB is compressed in your browser first, H.264 with sound kept, to land under the limit, then it uploads in chunks and attaches like a pasted link.

Message A is shorter: Saw your ads, free sample video attached below, then If you like it, I can make these for you daily or weekly. Open to a quick chat? The example record now sits last on Ready to send.
Product names also drop a leading store region code (EU, US, UK).

Message A now closes by offering more videos every day or every week and asking for a day and time to chat, instead of offering one more product. Product names drop store tags such as [Amazon #1], New Detail Page, Official and Best Seller. Rebuild all messages leaves anyone already sent Message A untouched.

Team permissions for Video Outreach: Admin, Team now has three tickboxes per member, Ready to send only (for whoever makes the videos), the whole module, and the Settings tab. Off unless ticked. A member sees only the tabs they were given and the server refuses everything else.

Activity gate: before a connection request goes out, the worker checks the person posted or commented on LinkedIn in the last 90 days. Active people earn 8 points and go first; inactive ones are held back with a note (set DM active 90d to Y to send anyway).
Every alert text is logged and Settings shows the last text sent, per person, with any failure.

Acceptance detection reads the whole connections list (paged, not just the first page) and also asks LinkedIn about each open request directly, 30 every 10 minutes: a 1st degree profile counts as accepted, an ignored or withdrawn invitation closes the request.

Test LinkedIn connection also reports how many sent invitations LinkedIn is holding and how many recent connections it returned. The example record's pretend events no longer count towards the daily and weekly caps.
The example record on Ready to send is now Klevaro, a real UK store, with its real products and photos, so demos look credible.
Look again on a WooCommerce store finished with an error after finding the products; fixed.

When a website blocks access the card says so plainly, and you can type the product or upload a photo of it (resized in the browser, kept on the prospect, shown on the card). WooCommerce reads wait longer for slow stores.
Look again on a card says what each store reader answered.

Product picking reads WooCommerce stores too (Shopify first, then WooCommerce, then the ads), and store readers identify as a normal browser so fewer stores refuse them. Ready to send cards show a Website link, a product set by hand shows as the product to film, and the attachment or link choice sits on one line.

The sample video can go out as an attachment that plays inside the LinkedIn message (now the default) or as a link. Paste the video link as before: the card finds the file behind it, checks the size straight away (must be under 20 MB) and only then lets you send. Settings, LinkedIn caps holds the default; each card can override it.

Ready to send: every lead has a green strip (New lead, brand, person, accepted when) so cards are clearly separate; when a store blocks readers the product comes from the ads' landing links, and a card with no product lets you type one by hand or look again.

Top-up runs search fresh keywords only (the originals kept returning the same brands), widen to neighbouring product categories once a run yields under five, and can run up to three times a day two hours apart while the queue is short.

Ready to send: the pasted video link drops into the message as you type, the example record is clearly marked as made up, and a Messages sent list shows every video and follow-up that went out with its reply.
Campaigns table: number columns trimmed so the action buttons sit inside the card.
Connection note test has a third arm, C: the request with no note at all. The three rotate evenly and Results shows each.

Connection note 50:50 test: automatic requests alternate note A (says what we do, offers the sample) and note B (mentions their product ads on Meta, asks to connect, no offer). Which note went out is on the prospect's history, and Results plus the daily report show sent, accepted, replied and positive per note. Switch it off in Settings, LinkedIn caps.
Campaigns table headers have space between them and wrap to two lines where needed.
Campaigns table fits the page without a left-right scroll: country and schedule sit under the campaign name, the waiting-for-video note is one short line, and the action column is narrower.

Score first, spend second: a brand only gets the paid Apollo lookup when its free Meta signals could still reach the priority cut-off. Weak brands are parked with the reason at a fraction of a penny, the per-brand ad count skips excluded and off-country brands, and the run table shows how many were parked without a lookup.

Campaigns table: the status pill no longer wraps (a style clash with the status line was stretching it), the notes sit under it, and the action buttons are stacked in one narrow column so Status has room.
Daily report tiles are clickable: waiting for a video and accepted open Ready to send, and each waiting brand name opens its own card; brands found, requests and replies open the prospects list.
Auto top-up keywords stay shopper intent: research terms (benefits, review, dosage, side effects, how to) are never added.

The queue tops itself up: when fewer brands than the daily cap are ready to request, the worker adds a few shopper keywords and starts one sourcing run a day on its own (campaign edit, Automation). Results and the daily report show how many brands are ready to request.

The LinkedIn queue no longer stalls behind a brand whose link is a company page: that brand is marked skipped with the reason (on the prospect and in the daily report) and the next brand is tried. Editing the link puts it back in the queue.
Message A leads with the product angle from their ads, adds the ad number only as a short clause and only when it came from a full count, and no longer tells the brand what it needs.

Product names in messages and texts drop the store's spec parts (weights, per gummy, pack counts), so a title like Core - Creatine Monohydrate Gummies - 1.5g per Gummy reads Core Creatine Monohydrate Gummies.
Static-ad brands no longer get the video point twice in one message.

Messages carry a proof line built from real numbers (new ads this month, ads live, static creative) so they read as researched, and Message A closes with a one-word-answer question that offers the next product on the shortlist.
Red count on the Ready to send tab and on the Video Outreach menu button: accepted connections waiting for a video plus follow-ups due today. Refreshes every two minutes.
A campaign that sets its own sender name signs with that name (the signature block is built from name and title unless you write your own).
Signature block under "Thanks,": name on one line, "Co-founder, ShekiPro.com" on the next, editable in Settings and per campaign. Brand written ShekiPro.com throughout.
Messages sign off "Aj, Co-founder at Shekipro" (sender title is a profile field). Rebuild all messages button in Settings rewrites every prospect's messages from the current profile.
A large photo of the product to film on the Ready to send card and the prospect page, with thumbnails for the second and third choice.
Ask AI has its own entry in the left menu under Video Outreach and its own tab, always one click away. The Help screen keeps a copy at the top.
Ready to send: with a LinkedIn provider connected the card shows Send on LinkedIn only; Copy and Mark Msg 1 sent sit behind a small "send by hand instead" link.

Show me an example on Ready to send: a made-up accepted connection with the shortlist, the draft and the URL box, so the screen can be understood before the first real one. Sending is off for it; one click removes it.

Ask AI on the Help and guide screen: answers from the guide and your live campaigns, remembers every question, drafts an FAQ entry you can add with one click (shown at the bottom of the guide), and logs feature ideas for the developer.

Film this, in order: a ranked shortlist of up to three products with the reason for each (named in their ads, on their homepage, matches the campaign) on the prospect page and the Ready to send card. The store is re-read the moment a connection is accepted so the pick reflects what they are pushing now.
Acceptance texts and emails carry a link that opens that brand's Ready to send card with the video box ready.
Daily report email every morning after 8am UK (brands found, requests, acceptances with times, videos sent, replies, what is waiting for you), and the same numbers on the Results tab.
Help and guide in the left menu under Video Outreach, with exact click paths, times of day and a step-by-step campaign setup.
Connection requests go out at a random 10 to 30 minute gap, never the same gap twice in a row. Settings shows when the next one is due.
Quick check on the Prospects list: the four hand-checked signals for every brand in one table with dropdowns and a LinkedIn link per contact. One Save re-scores every row you changed.
Acceptance alerts now read "new ShekiPro connection" in the text and the email subject.
Campaigns table reads as a funnel: Prospects, Requested, Connected, Videos sent (with how many accepted leads still wait for a video), Positive replies, Other replies.
Campaigns table tidied: one neat row of buttons, alternating row shading, Requested, Connected, Positive replies and Other replies columns.
Help opens inside Video Outreach as its own tab, with the week-by-week flow, where you step in, and FAQs.
Reset outreach button on a prospect: back to Not contacted after a test, keeping the event trail.
New-lead SMS and email when a connection is accepted ("Aryan, you have a new lead for ShekiPro..."), addressed by first name; Send a test text button in Settings.
Settings shows set or not set for each of the three Unipile variables and for the email sender.
SMS reply alerts: add mobiles in Settings and get a text on Positive and Question replies (or every reply) saying who replied, via which channel, what they want and what to do next.
Replies are read as Positive, Negative, Question or Neutral: a coloured chip on the prospect and in the list, the email alert subject says which, and a one-line summary of what they want.
Record a reply box on the prospect page for replies you received yourself.

No more fading toasts or pop-up messages in Video Outreach: one bold status line under the tabs stays on screen (green done, red problem) until the next action. Confirm boxes remain only before spending credits, sending, or deleting.
Refresh ad counts ends with a clear pop-up, and says so when everything was already counted.
Help bubbles on the campaign page sections: Run now, Ad counts (Refresh), Import prospects and Runs.
Refresh ad counts shows progress from the first click: the brand it is on and its new ad count.
Refresh ad counts button on the campaign page: re-pulls each brand's own ads (newest 30) and re-scores, for runs whose count pass was skipped.
Prospects remember their Meta page id so recounts are exact.
Help page with a menu and sub-sections (the 📖 Help tab in Video Outreach): how it all works, how to use it, what is automatic, costs, troubleshooting and the version history.
Fixed: a run could fail to save when an ad's text was cut in the middle of an emoji (Postgres rejected the JSON). Text is now cut on whole characters and broken characters are stripped before saving.
Trigger event is set automatically when a brand is hiring a marketing role or has launched 10 or more ads this month, with the reason in the trigger note.
Apollo people search moved to the current endpoint (the old one is refused for API callers), so contacts come back.
Apify per-brand count pass sends the page URL and settings in the shape the actor expects.
A run is stepped by one worker at a time (heartbeat), so the cron and the screen never process the same brands twice.
Merchandise is never picked as the sample product while a real product exists.
Live runs count each brand's own ads (newest 30) after the keyword search, so Active Meta ads, video share and new ads are real, not a sample.
Brand names come from the company record, not the ad page (which can be a creator or a blog).
The decision maker is enriched once per brand so the full name and LinkedIn link are present.
A store that is not on Shopify is kept (product picked by hand) instead of disqualified, per the spec's feed-or-cart rule.
Product picks prefer real products matching the campaign keywords over merchandise like tees and sets.
Live Meta Ad Library pulls run in the background on Apify and the run waits for them (a real pull takes 1 to 5 minutes), so runs no longer hit the 60-second limit.
Runs keep a sample of each provider's raw answer so field mapping can be checked.
Prospect filters sit side by side instead of stretching across the page.
Marking Msg 1 sent by hand now schedules Follow-up 1 (3 days) and Follow-up 2 (7 days) like the email and LinkedIn sends do; a reply or Dead cancels them.
Prospects table condensed to 8 readable columns (priority, number, score and tier in one cell; links and connection in one) so headers no longer break letter by letter.

Prospect field help rewritten: each explains what the fact is, how to read the number and the points it earns. Labels renamed: Other paid channels (count), Growth signals (count), Creative gap (points).
Campaign, run, prospect and results tables fit the screen and wrap instead of scrolling left to right.
A small ? next to every field in the campaign form and the prospect page explains what it is and how to use it (hover or tap).
App files are no longer cached by the browser, so a new version shows on a normal refresh.
Run now shows a Running state straight away: pulsing tiles, a spinner and a line saying which brand is being scored; the button is disabled until the run finishes.
Run now is the first button on the Campaigns list and the buttons wrap instead of scrolling off the edge.
Version number bottom-left is clickable and shows this history.
Changelog kept in the repo (CHANGELOG.md) and in the app.
Clear prospects on a run now reports what it really removed and falls back to the run's time window.
AI observations cleaned so messages never read 'Came across Came across' or end with two full stops.
Broken product or ad images show a grey 'no image' tile.
Traffic proxy row in the score breakdown reads in words.
Version number pinned to the bottom-left corner.
Brands with no named contact are kept and flagged 'find one by hand' (tracker rule) instead of disqualified.
Delete a prospect from its page; Clear prospects on a finished run.

Video Outreach Phases 2 to 5: Apollo and Meta Ad Library sourcing, Shopify products and the photo rule, email sends with open tracking, resumable runs with progress tiles, scheduled campaigns, keyword suggester and presets, Results, weight tuning, template sets, plan gating, LinkedIn automation behind a provider switch.
Fixed: sourced prospects failed to save (duplicate column).
Version stamp added to the sidebar.
Video Outreach Phase 1: scoring engine, v12 tracker import, campaigns and prospects screens, prospect detail with messages, connection and stage tracking. 107 tests.
